newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland sees good chance to meet EMU criteria 1997.
newsitem.headline: Finland sees good chance to meet EMU criteria 1997.

text.p: Finland is well placed to meet in 1997 the entry criteria for the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union, the government said on Tuesday.
"Finland has good prospects for fulfilling the convergence criteria in 1997," the government said in an updated convergence programme.
"At present, Finland meets the inflation and interest rate criteria, and the value of the markka has remained stable for a long time," it said.
The public sector deficit would fall below the three percent limit already this year, and go on shrinking in 1997.
"The ratio of the general government deficit to GDP will be about 1.4 percent in 1997," the government said. This year's deficit is projected at 2.9 percent.
The convergence programme walks hand in hand with Finland's state budget proposal which is based on 3.9 percent gross domestic product growth next year.
"Even under the circumstances of slow growth, the deficit criterion would be met," the programme stated.
"Under favourable economic developments, expenditure cuts will suffice to bring the central government indebtedness into decline," it said.
And for good measure it added: "If future developments in public finance threaten to deviate from the line described in this programme, the government will take the necessary measures."
These would be designed to safeguard the attainment of fiscal policy targets, the most important one being EMU.
"Finland's objective is to fulfil the convergence criteria for EMU so that Finland could participate in the Economic and Monetary Union right at the beginning in 1999," the government said.

More broadly, economic policy aims at sustainable economic growth, a permanently slow rate of inflation, bringing central government indebtedness into decline and alleviating the unemployment problem.
"The economic policy aiming at meeting the convergence criteria also contributes to the reduction of unemployment," the government said.

Good competitiveness and low real interest rates were key conditions for sustainable economic growth. "In the lowering of real interest rates, a key role is played by the current account surplus," it said.
Finnish inflation, although speeding up to 1.5 percent in 1997 from 0.8 percent this year according to the finance ministry's forecast, would "continue to be slow," it said.

Modest inflation and a current account surplus seen at 21.2 billion markka or 3.5 percent of GDP in 1997 gave the government reason to say: "Finland has good prospects for adhering to a stable value of money even in the future."
The convergence programme gave the following figures (pct):
Public sector deficit/GDP 2.9 1.4 0.5
Public sector debt/GDP 61.8 61.0 59.9
Inflation +0.8 +1.5 +2.0
10-year bond yield 7.3 7.3 7.3
C/A surplus/GDP 3.5 3.5 2.5
Unemployment rate 16.4 15.4 14.0
